sources.entry: Notifo - Multichannel notification server with support for Email, Mobile Push, Web Push, SMS, messaging and a javascript plugin. MIT C#

summary.one_liner: Notifo is a multi-channel notification server that sends messages to users by email, SMS, mobile push, web push, messaging apps, webhooks and a web overlay, built with ASP.NET Core and React.
summary.what_it_does: Users subscribe to topic paths such as clothes/shoes/nike, and your backend publishes events to specific topic paths. Notifo matches events to subscriptions, applies per-subscription channel preferences, and delivers through providers such as SMTP, Amazon SES, Twilio, Firebase, Telegram, Discord and VAPID web push. Notifications can carry a confirmation mode (None, Explicit or Seen) so that users who already confirmed or viewed a notification are not sent it again, with an optional delay before sending. Queues and schedulers handle retries, and delivery, seen and confirmed states are tracked. It includes a REST API with OpenAPI docs, a management UI for templates, users, subscriptions and apps, MJML and Liquid email templates, and an embeddable JavaScript SDK that shows a notification overlay in a web app.
use_cases: send email, SMS and push notifications from one API
notify users about project or task updates
in-app notification overlay for a web application
send order or news alerts to subscribers
track whether users have seen or confirmed a notification
how_to_run: Open the domain in a browser and create the first administrator account
Read the 'Before you go live' guide before exposing the instance (replace the shipped web push key pair and social login credentials)
notable: Topic-path subscriptions with per-subscription channel preferences
Confirmation modes (None, Explicit, Seen) suppress notifications users have already acted on
Multiple database backends: MongoDB, or MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server via Entity Framework
Embeddable JavaScript SDK for in-app notification overlays
caveats: The shipped defaults include a public web push key pair and social login credentials belonging to notifo.io, so they must be replaced before going live
Self-hosting requires configuring a domain, TLS and a database, and the README points to several separate docs for this
Some provider and channel coverage is still listed as open work, such as voice and mobile push test apps
